Delegation is fully down: every named template is unresolvable, and the fallback agent inherits my toolless configuration (no file-edit, no shell). I cannot dispatch implementation work, and I have no execution tools myself by design. Stopping here rather than burning spawns.

## Completed and committed to `main` (`4be3ae17`, hook clean, nothing leaked)

Worktrees now bootstrap from **local** `main`. Root cause was concrete: `origin` is the GitHub remote, local `main` (`d44b8efa`) was *ahead* of it, and the recorded submodule commits were never pushed — so `fetch origin` + `submodule update` left [`memory-viewers`](memory-viewers ), [`viewer-api`](viewer-api ), and [`memory-kernel`](memory-kernel ) as bare .git stubs and broke the cargo workspace load on doc-viewer.

- worktree.sh — `cmd_new` branches straight from local `main` (no fetch, no `origin/main` ff-merge); submodules populate **offline** via per-submodule `git worktree add --detach <recorded-sha>`, which avoids repointing the shared `.git/modules/<name>` `core.worktree` that was emptying the main checkout; `cmd_rebase` rebases onto local `main`; `cmd_remove` now tears down the per-submodule worktrees it creates. `git submodule deinit` is never executed — the two grep hits are usage text and a warning comment.
- Docs realigned so prose can't drift from the script: branch-worktree.instructions.md, orchestrator.agent.md, implement.agent.md, commit.agent.md.
- Tracking ticket `503b9711`.

## Worktree repaired and independently verified

f3c2b8a9-install-ctl on `agent/f3c2b8a9-install-ctl`, rebased to `4be3ae17`, clean tree, all 5 submodules populated (12–18 entries each), `cargo metadata --no-deps` OK. Main checkout unharmed — 15 pre-existing dirty paths untouched, no submodule entries dirty, `cargo metadata` OK. The rewritten `new`, `rebase`, and `remove` paths have each now run for real.

## install-ctl progress (uncommitted, safe in the worktree)

- tools/install/artifacts.toml — 25 artifacts (24 Rust binaries + `ticket-vscode`) across 5 categories, read at **runtime**.
- `tools/install/install-ctl` crate, added to the root workspace; `--list` and `--dry-run install <selection>` work, mirroring install-tools.sh selection syntax.
- Acceptance criteria **3 and 4 met** — AC3 proven empirically (registry edited → `--list` changed with no rebuild → reverted clean). Build, `cargo metadata`, and clippy all pass.

## Blocker

`runSubagent` cannot resolve any workspace template (`Implement Agent`, `Explore Agent`, `Default` all now fail; the last two succeeded earlier in this session), and the unnamed fallback has no edit or shell tools. Nothing is in a broken state — the committed work is complete and the worktree is healthy — but the remaining units are stalled:

1. Port `process.rs`/`shell.rs` into install-ctl + real install with process-stopping (**AC1**, the headline fix, and **AC2**)
2. Add `start`/`prepare` so the 8 VS Code viewer tasks keep working (**AC5**)
3. Rewrite consumers: 28 Makefile.toml refs, tasks.json, `install_contract_sync.rs` (**AC6**), and shrink install-tools.sh/install-extensions.sh to bootstrap-and-invoke
4. Delete viewer-ctl (needs a submodule branch + commit + gitlink bump) and `cargo build --release` (**AC7**)

Tell me when the agent surface is back and I'll resume at unit 1 — or if you'd prefer, I can hand you the exact per-unit prompts to run directly.

---

Try again now and continue

DESCRIPTION:
Problem

The repository's `install-tools.sh` is failing to overwrite binaries when those binaries are held open by running processes (notably on Windows where an .exe is locked by the process). Root cause verified: `install-tools.sh` (line ~324) runs `cargo install --path ... --bin ... --force` with no mechanism to detect and stop a running process holding the executable open, so the install fails when the process does not exit and the OS prevents overwrite.

Decisions (already made)

1. The new binary is named `install-ctl`.
2. Organization: generalize `viewer-ctl` into `install-ctl`. This is one tool; viewer entries become ordinary managed-artifact entries alongside general tool binaries. This is NOT a shared-crate extraction and NOT a copy.
3. The managed-artifact registry will be a committed TOML file mirroring the shape of the existing `viewer-ctl.toml`.
4. The shell surface collapses to a single bootstrap script: `install-tools.sh` and `install-extensions.sh` are removed; the remaining script only builds/installs `install-ctl` and forwards args to it.

Research facts (verified)

- `install-tools.sh` (369 lines, repo root) installs 24 artifacts across helper tools, CLI tools, MCP tools, and four viewers. Flags: positional names, `--tool`, `--tools`, `--mcp`, `--all`, `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--no-force`, `-h/--help`; env `INSTALL_TOOLS` used only when the CLI selects nothing.
- `install-extensions.sh` (351 lines, repo root) installs `ticket-vscode` (from `memory-api/tools/ticket-vscode`) and exposes similar CLI flags; VS Code extension install logic is already implemented in Rust under `viewer-ctl`.
- `viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs` already exposes the needed process-management helpers: `pids_on_port`, `pids_by_image_name`, `kill_process`, `process_exists`, and `print_process_info`. `pids_by_image_name` is sufficient for non-server binaries like `mcp-toolmon` and `copilot-capture-hook`. `kill_process` uses `taskkill` on Windows.
- `viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/extension.rs` and `server.rs` already cover extension installation and build/install workflow patterns (cargo build, copy release binaries, fallback to `cargo install --path`), so much of `install-extensions.sh` and `install-tools.sh` behavior is already present in Rust.
- `viewer-ctl` has a committed TOML registry (`viewer-ctl.toml`) and a `viewer-api/viewer-ctl.toml` mirror; the same model will be used for `install-ctl`.

Approach / Generalization

- Implement `install-ctl` as a Rust CLI (relocating and adapting `viewer-ctl` functionality) that:
  - Reads a committed TOML registry (repo-root `install-ctl.toml` or re-using `viewer-ctl.toml` shape) describing managed artifact kinds: managed server, general tool binary, VS Code extension, frontend, and task.
  - For binary installs, when the destination executable is held by a running process, `install-ctl` discovers the culprit using `pids_by_image_name` and stops it (graceful stop, then forced kill if configured), reporting the stopped PID(s) in the CLI output.
  - Preserves `--dry-run`, `--list`, and selection semantics from `install-tools.sh` and `install-extensions.sh`.
  - Provides `install`, `uninstall`, `list`, `prepare`, and lifecycle commands similar to `viewer-ctl` but generalized for tools (viewers become just one artifact-kind).
  - Keeps registry additions editable without Rust recompile: registry is a committed TOML file and `install-ctl` reads it at runtime.
  - Replace the two shell scripts with a single bootstrap installer script that only builds/installs `install-ctl` and forwards args to it.

Acceptance Criteria (concrete & verifiable)

1. Installing a tool binary whose process is currently running succeeds: `install-ctl` discovers the holder via `pids_by_image_name`, stops it (graceful then forced as needed), installs the new binary, and reports which PID(s) were stopped. Demonstration: start `mcp-toolmon` locally, run `install-ctl install mcp-toolmon`, observe `install-ctl` stops the running process and the install completes (cargo can replace the executable).

2. All artifacts previously installable by `install-tools.sh` (the 24 listed artifacts) and `install-extensions.sh` (`ticket-vscode`) are installable via `install-ctl` and appear in `install-ctl --list`.

3. The artifact registry is a committed TOML file in the repo; adding an artifact entry requires no Rust recompile and is reflected in `install-ctl --list` after editing the TOML.

4. `--dry-run`, selection semantics, and `--list` are preserved: `install-ctl --dry-run` shows the planned actions without performing them; `install-ctl --list` enumerates available artifacts and categories.

5. The eight `.vscode/tasks.json` viewer tasks that currently call `viewer-ctl start/prepare` continue to work (either by `install-ctl` providing compatible `start/prepare` shims for managed viewers, or by keeping `viewer-ctl` as a thin compatibility shim that forwards into `install-ctl`).

7. `cargo build --release` for the whole workspace succeeds after any crate relocation and workspace-member update (e.g., moving `viewer-ctl` crate to `install-ctl` or adding `install-ctl` as a workspace member).

Implementation notes / non-goals

- Do NOT attempt to make `install-ctl` a shared crate copy of `viewer-ctl`; the intent is to generalize and relocate logic, not duplicate code.
- Tests that assert `viewer-ctl` binary name should be updated to accept `install-ctl` or a compatibility shim unless a thin wrapper remains.

CONFIG_CONTENTS:
# viewer-ctl component registry
#
# Lists every server, frontend, extension, and task viewer-ctl can manage.
# All paths are relative to the repository root (the directory containing
# this file).
#
# Adding a new viewer:
#   1. Add a [[server]] entry with name + cargo package + port.
#   2. Add a [[frontend]] entry that links to the server via `serves`.
#   3. Optional: add [[extension]] or [[task]] entries.
#
# Lifecycle commands:
#   viewer-ctl list                       # show all components
#   viewer-ctl status [<name>]            # show running state
#   viewer-ctl build   <name>             # build artifacts (no install)
#   viewer-ctl install <name>             # install artifacts to install_root
#   viewer-ctl start   <server>           # launch server
#   viewer-ctl stop    <server>           # kill process on server's port
#   viewer-ctl restart <server>           # stop + start
#   viewer-ctl task    <name>             # run a named multi-step task

[defaults]
# Where installed frontend bundles live. Each frontend is installed to
# <frontend_install_root>/<frontend.name>/. The path supports a leading
# `~` which expands to the user's home directory.
#
# Servers receive STATIC_DIR=<frontend_install_root>/<linked frontend name>
# when launched via `viewer-ctl start`.
frontend_install_root = "~/.context-engine/static"

# ── Servers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[server]]
name = "doc-viewer"
package = "doc-viewer"
port = 3001
source_dir = "memory-viewers/doc-viewer"

[[server]]
name = "log-viewer"
package = "log-viewer"
port = 3000
source_dir = "memory-viewers/log-viewer"
start_args = ["--static"]

[[server]]
name = "ticket-viewer"
package = "ticket-viewer"
port = 3002
source_dir = "memory-viewers/ticket-viewer"

[[server]]
name = "spec-viewer"
package = "spec-viewer"
port = 4002
source_dir = "memory-viewers/spec-viewer"

# ── Frontends ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[frontend]]
name = "doc-viewer"
serves = "doc-viewer"
source_dir = "memory-viewers/doc-viewer/frontend/dioxus"
build_cmd = ["trunk", "build", "--release"]
build_output = "memory-viewers/doc-viewer/frontend/dioxus/dist"
extra_assets = ["memory-viewers/doc-viewer/frontend/dioxus/public"]

[[frontend.prebuild]]
dir = "viewer-api/frontend/ts"
cmd = ["npm", "install"]
condition = "missing:node_modules"

[[frontend]]
name = "log-viewer"
serves = "log-viewer"
source_dir = "memory-viewers/log-viewer/frontend/dioxus"
build_cmd = ["trunk", "build", "--release"]
build_output = "memory-viewers/log-viewer/frontend/dioxus/dist"
extra_assets = ["memory-viewers/log-viewer/frontend/dioxus/public"]

[[frontend.prebuild]]
dir = "viewer-api/frontend/ts"
cmd = ["npm", "install"]
condition = "missing:node_modules"

[[frontend.prebuild]]
dir = "memory-viewers/log-viewer/frontend"
cmd = ["npm", "install"]
condition = "missing:node_modules"

[[frontend]]
name = "ticket-viewer"
serves = "ticket-viewer"
source_dir = "tools/viewer/ticket-viewer/frontend/dioxus"
build_cmd = ["trunk", "build", "--release", "--features", "profile-browser"]
build_output = "tools/viewer/ticket-viewer/frontend/dioxus/dist"
extra_assets = ["tools/viewer/ticket-viewer/frontend/dioxus/public"]

[[frontend]]
name = "spec-viewer"
serves = "spec-viewer"
source_dir = "tools/viewer/spec-viewer/frontend/dioxus"
build_cmd = ["trunk", "build", "--release", "--features", "profile-browser"]
build_output = "tools/viewer/spec-viewer/frontend/dioxus/dist"
extra_assets = ["tools/viewer/spec-viewer/frontend/dioxus/public"]

# ── Extensions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[extension]]
name = "ticket-vscode"
kind = "vscode"
source_dir = "memory-api/tools/ticket-vscode"
package_json = "package.json"
build_cmd = ["npm", "run", "compile"]

# Helper to print grouped results
print_grouped() {
  local results="$1"
  if [ -z "$results" ]; then
    return
  fi
  # iterate unique files
  echo "$results" | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u | while read -r file; do
    # count hits
    cnt=$(echo "$results" | grep -F "^$file:" | wc -l | tr -d " ")
    echo "$file = $cnt"
    if [ "$cnt" -le 6 ]; then
      echo "$results" | grep -F "^$file:" | sed -E "s|^$file:([0-9]+):(.*)|  \1: \2|"
    else
      lines=$(echo "$results" | grep -F "^$file:")
      N=$(echo "$lines" | wc -l | tr -d " ")
      idx1=1
      idx2=$(( (N+2)/3 ))
      idx3=$(( (2*N+2)/3 ))
      idx4=$N
      # ensure unique increasing indices
      # clamp
      [ "$idx2" -lt 1 ] && idx2=1
      [ "$idx3" -lt 1 ] && idx3=1
      [ "$idx4" -lt 1 ] && idx4=1
      # print selected
      echo "$lines" | sed -n "${idx1}p" | sed -E "s|^$file:([0-9]+):(.*)|  \1: \2|"
      echo "$lines" | sed -n "${idx2}p" | sed -E "s|^$file:([0-9]+):(.*)|  \1: \2|"
      echo "$lines" | sed -n "${idx3}p" | sed -E "s|^$file:([0-9]+):(.*)|  \1: \2|"
      echo "$lines" | sed -n "${idx4}p" | sed -E "s|^$file:([0-9]+):(.*)|  \1: \2|"
    fi
  done
}

# Compose final output in required shape
printf "VIEWER_CTL_REFS:\n"
if [ -z "$results1" ]; then
  # show nothing under header
  :
else
  print_grouped "$results1"
fi

printf "\nINSTALL_SCRIPT_REFS:\n"
if [ -z "$results2" ]; then
  :
else
  print_grouped "$results2"
fi

# Check stray files at worktree root
strays=""
for f in install_script_refs.txt vc_refs.txt; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    sz=$(stat -c%s "$f" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$f" )
    if [ -n "$strays" ]; then strays+=", "; fi
    strays+="$f=$sz"
  else
    if [ -n "$strays" ]; then strays+=", "; fi
    strays+="$f=none"
  fi
done

printf "\nSTRAY_FILES: %s\n" "$strays"

# No truncation logic applied here
printf "TRUNCATED: no\n"
'

use std::{
    fs,
    path::{
        Path,
        PathBuf,
    },
};

const INSTALL_CONTRACT_SLUG: &str =
    "memory-api/install-contracts/cli-and-viewer-installation";
const README_RULE_PATH: &str =
    ".rule/rules/84278ede-0aaa-4382-83db-e6ee5d80106c/body.md";

fn memory_api_root() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("../../..")
        .canonicalize()
        .expect("memory-api root should exist")
}

fn install_contract_dir() -> PathBuf {
    let specs_root = memory_api_root().join(".spec").join("specs");
    let entries =
        fs::read_dir(&specs_root).expect("specs directory should be readable");

    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        let spec_toml = path.join("spec.toml");
        let Ok(contents) = fs::read_to_string(&spec_toml) else {
            continue;
        };
        if contents.contains(&format!("slug = \"{INSTALL_CONTRACT_SLUG}\"")) {
            return path;
        }
    }

    panic!(
        "could not find install contract spec for slug {INSTALL_CONTRACT_SLUG}"
    );
}

fn section(name: &str) -> String {
    fs::read_to_string(
        install_contract_dir()
            .join("sections")
            .join(format!("{name}.md")),
    )
    .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("missing section {name}"))
}

fn normalize_newlines(input: &str) -> String {
    input.replace("\r\n", "\n")
}

#[test]
fn readme_install_flow_section_matches_readme_rule_entry() {
    let expected = section("readme-install-flow");
    let actual =
        fs::read_to_string(memory_api_root().join(README_RULE_PATH)).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(normalize_newlines(&actual), normalize_newlines(&expected));
}

#[test]
fn install_contract_sections_record_cli_and_viewer_matrix() {
    let cli = section("cli-scenario-matrix");
    for scenario in ["CLI-01", "CLI-02", "CLI-03", "CLI-04", "CLI-05"] {
        assert!(cli.contains(scenario), "missing CLI scenario {scenario}");
    }
    assert!(cli.contains("cargo install --path tools/cli/rule-cli --bin rule"));
    assert!(cli.contains("cargo uninstall rule-cli"));
    assert!(cli.contains("rule list"));
    assert!(cli.contains("rule create --title \"Install validation rule\""));
    assert!(cli.contains("spec create --title \"Install validation spec\""));
    assert!(cli.contains("ticket create --title \"Install validation ticket\" --type tracker-improvement"));
    assert!(cli.contains("audit run ."));

    let viewer = section("viewer-install-boundary");
    for scenario in ["VIEW-01", "VIEW-02", "VIEW-03", "VIEW-04"] {
        assert!(
            viewer.contains(scenario),
            "missing viewer scenario {scenario}"
        );
    }
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install doc-viewer --kind server"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install doc-viewer --kind frontend"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install log-viewer --kind server"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install log-viewer --kind frontend"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install ticket-viewer --kind server"));
    assert!(
        viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install ticket-viewer --kind frontend")
    );
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install spec-viewer --kind server"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("viewer-ctl install spec-viewer --kind frontend"));
    assert!(viewer.contains("No first-class uninstall command exists"));
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

run_filtered_command() {
    local label=$1
    shift
    local status_file
    local last_stdout_line=""
    local saw_stdout=0
    local command_status=1
    local interactive=0

    if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
        interactive=1
    fi

    status_file=$(mktemp)

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        saw_stdout=1
        last_stdout_line=$line

        if [[ $interactive -eq 1 ]]; then
            printf '\r\033[2K    %s: %s' "$label" "$line"
        fi
    done < <(
        (
            "$@"
            printf '%s\n' "$?" > "$status_file"
        ) 2> >(cat >&2)
    )

    if [[ -s "$status_file" ]]; then
        command_status=$(<"$status_file")
    fi

    rm -f "$status_file"

    if [[ $saw_stdout -eq 1 ]]; then
        if [[ $interactive -eq 1 ]]; then
            printf '\r\033[2K    %s: %s\n' "$label" "$last_stdout_line"
        else
            printf '    %s: %s\n' "$label" "$last_stdout_line"
        fi
    fi

    return "$command_status"
}

print_joined_items() {
    local first=1
    local item

    for item in "$@"; do
        if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then
            printf '%s' "$item"
            first=0
        else
            printf ', %s' "$item"
        fi
    done
}

installer_print_summary() {
    local requested_count=$1
    local succeeded_name=$2
    local failed_name=$3
    local retry_prefix=${4:-}
    local help_command=${5:-}
    local -n succeeded_ref=$succeeded_name
    local -n failed_ref=$failed_name

    printf '\nInstall summary: requested=%d, succeeded=%d, failed=%d\n' \
        "$requested_count" "${#succeeded_ref[@]}" "${#failed_ref[@]}"

    if [[ ${#succeeded_ref[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        printf 'Succeeded: '
        print_joined_items "${succeeded_ref[@]}"
        printf '\n'
    fi

    if [[ ${#failed_ref[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        printf 'Failed: '
        print_joined_items "${failed_ref[@]}"
        printf '\n\n'

        if [[ -n "$retry_prefix" ]]; then
            printf 'Retry failed installs with:\n'
            printf '  %s' "$retry_prefix"
            local item
            for item in "${failed_ref[@]}"; do
                printf ' %q' "$item"
            done
            printf '\n\n'
        fi

        if [[ -n "$help_command" ]]; then
            printf 'For more options, run:\n'
            printf '  %s\n' "$help_command"
        fi

        return 1
    fi

    return 0
}

data_json.reasoningText:
I'm seeing that `gen-types` and `vscode-ext` don't actually exist as CLI subcommands in viewer-ctl—they're just stale references lingering in the Makefile. Rather than try to fix them, I'll rename the command to `install-ctl` for clarity while keeping the arguments as-is, and note that these were pre-existing broken tasks.

Now I need to map out all the exact replacements for Makefile.toml. The `build-viewer-ctl` task itself (which compiles the viewer-ctl crate with cargo) should stay untouched since that's building the binary, not invoking it—the objective is specifically about repointing tasks that *call* viewer-ctl, not the build task for the crate itself.

The real changes are in lines 82, 87, 92, and 97 where the frontend doc/log/ticket/spec-viewer tasks invoke viewer-ctl directly; those need to switch to calling `install-ctl viewer` instead. Then there's the install-viewer-ctl task itself that needs updating. The path "viewer-api/tools/viewer/viewer-ctl" in the Makefile is likely incorrect and doesn't match the actual location, but fixing it is out of scope since I'm only adding the install-ctl task. The install-viewer-ctl task itself doesn't directly invoke viewer-ctl as a command—it uses cargo—so it wouldn't have matched my earlier grep search for "viewer-ctl" as the command, though the task name and path references did appear in those results.

Now I'm looking at the actual tasks that need rewiring: lines 158, 163, 168, 173 for the install-doc/log/ticket/spec-viewer tasks, and lines 185, 190, 195, 200 for the start-doc/log/ticket/spec-viewer tasks. These all currently run viewer-ctl with install or start subcommands, and I need to change them to use install-ctl instead with the arguments reordered.

For the start tasks, I can use the top-level "start" alias directly without nesting "viewer" since that's how install-ctl is designed. The stop tasks on lines 210, 215, 220, 225 don't have a top-level alias, so they'll need the full "viewer stop" nesting. I'm also preserving the gen-types subcommand on line 244 as-is since it's a pre-existing dead command, and I'm about to handle the build-vscode-ext task on line 253. I'm tallying up all the viewer-ctl references across the file to make sure I'm only changing the command invocations and comments, not the task definitions themselves like the build-viewer-ctl task header or the install-viewer-ctl task that I'm intentionally leaving alone.

Now I'm ready to start making the replacements using multi_replace_string_in_file, making sure each context is unique enough to target the right lines.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Thin bootstrap-and-invoke wrapper around install-ctl (tools/install/install-ctl).
# All install mechanics (path/bin resolution, process-stop-before-install,
# CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation) live in install-ctl and its runtime-read
# tools/install/artifacts.toml registry; this script only preserves the
# existing CLI selection syntax and per-tool summary/exit-code behavior.

script_dir=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
repo_root=$script_dir
common_install_helpers="$repo_root/tools/install/common.sh"

if [[ ! -f "$common_install_helpers" ]]; then
    printf 'error: missing shared installer helpers: %s\n' "$common_install_helpers" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# shellcheck source=tools/install/common.sh
source "$common_install_helpers"

tool_names=(
    viewer-ctl
    doc-viewer
    log-viewer
    spec-viewer
    ticket-viewer
    copilot-capture-hook
    ticket-cli
    spec-cli
    audit-cli
    rule-cli
    feedback-cli
    session-cli
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
)

mcp_tool_names=(
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
    log-viewer
)

# Locate install-ctl: prefer an already-installed binary on PATH, otherwise
# run it straight from source via cargo (no separate build step required).
resolve_install_ctl() {
    if command -v install-ctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'install-ctl\n'
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'cargo run --manifest-path %q/tools/install/install-ctl/Cargo.toml --quiet --\n' "$repo_root"
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./install-tools.sh [options] [tool ...]

Install selected workspace tools with cargo install --path.

This script installs only deliverables built from this repository. External
toolchain dependencies are handled by ./install-deps.sh.

Options:
  --tool <name>       Install one tool; repeatable.
  --tools <a,b,c>     Install a comma-separated list of tools.
  --mcp               Install all MCP binaries configured for VS Code.
  --all               Install all supported tools.
  --list              Print supported tools and exit.
  --dry-run           Print the cargo install commands without running them.
  --no-force          Do not pass --force to cargo install.
  -h, --help          Show this help text.

EOF

    printf 'Supported tools:\n'
    print_supported_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    printf '\nMCP tools (--mcp):\n'
    print_mcp_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    cat <<'EOF'

Environment:
  INSTALL_TOOLS       Comma-separated tool list used when no tools are passed.

Examples:
  ./install-tools.sh
  ./install-tools.sh spec-cli ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool viewer-ctl --tool ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool doc-viewer --tool log-viewer --tool spec-viewer --tool ticket-viewer
  ./install-tools.sh --tool audit-cli --tool rule-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool mcp-toolmon
  ./install-tools.sh --mcp
  INSTALL_TOOLS="rule-cli,spec-cli" ./install-tools.sh --dry-run
EOF
}

print_supported_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

print_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

contains_tool() {
    local needle=$1
    shift

    local item
    for item in "$@"; do
        if [[ "$item" == "$needle" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    return 1
}

append_tool() {
    local tool=$1

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${tool_names[@]}"; then
        printf 'error: unsupported tool: %s\n' "$tool" >&2
        printf 'supported tools:\n' >&2
        print_supported_tools >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${selected_tools[@]}"; then
        selected_tools+=("$tool")
    fi
}

append_csv_tools() {
    local csv=$1
    local item

    IFS=',' read -r -a csv_tools <<< "$csv"
    for item in "${csv_tools[@]}"; do
        item=${item//[[:space:]]/}
        [[ -n "$item" ]] || continue
        append_tool "$item"
    done
}

append_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
}

selected_tools=()
installed_tools=()
failed_tools=()
force_install=1
dry_run=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --tool)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tool requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_tool "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --tools)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tools requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_csv_tools "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --all)
            selected_tools=()
            for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
                append_tool "$tool"
            done
            shift
            ;;
        --mcp)
            append_mcp_tools
            shift
            ;;
        --list)
            print_supported_tools
            exit 0
            ;;
        --dry-run)
            dry_run=1
            shift
            ;;
        --no-force)
            force_install=0
            shift
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            usage
            exit 0
            ;;
        --)
            shift
            while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
                append_tool "$1"
                shift
            done
            break
            ;;
        -*)
            printf 'error: unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        *)
            append_tool "$1"
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 && -n "${INSTALL_TOOLS:-}" ]]; then
    append_csv_tools "$INSTALL_TOOLS"
fi

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
fi

install_ctl_cmd=$(resolve_install_ctl)

install_one() {
    local tool=$1
    local failed=0
    local -a install_ctl_args=(install "$tool")

    if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args+=(--no-force)
    fi
    if [[ $dry_run -eq 1 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args=(--dry-run "${install_ctl_args[@]}")
    fi

    printf '==> %s\n' "$tool"

    if ! (
        cd "$repo_root"
        eval "$install_ctl_cmd" "\${install_ctl_args[@]@Q}"
    ); then
        failed=1
    fi

    if [[ $failed -eq 0 ]]; then
        installed_tools+=("$tool")
        return 0
    fi

    failed_tools+=("$tool")
    printf 'error: install failed for %s\n' "$tool" >&2
    return 1
}

for tool in "${selected_tools[@]}"; do
    install_one "$tool" || true
done

retry_prefix="./install-tools.sh"
if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
    retry_prefix="$retry_prefix --no-force"
fi

if ! installer_print_summary "${#selected_tools[@]}" installed_tools failed_tools "$retry_prefix" "./install-tools.sh --help"; then
    exit 1
fi

But I'm noticing the old install-tools.sh included "log-viewer" in its mcp_tool_names array, even though log-viewer is categorized as "viewer" in artifacts.toml, not "mcp" — I need to figure out if that's intentional or an oversight.

Since install-ctl's category system can't select both "mcp" and "log-viewer" together without explicit tokens, I'll keep the hard-coded mcp_tool_names array in my wrapper script itself. This lets me build an explicit comma-separated list of all 13 tool IDs (the 12 from mcp category plus log-viewer) and pass it directly to `install-ctl install <csv>`, which handles comma-separated selections. This way the wrapper stays thin — it just maps flags to a selection list and delegates to install-ctl.

For the new install-tools.sh design, I'm keeping the tool_names and mcp_tool_names arrays unchanged for validation and listing, but dropping the tool_path and tool_bin functions since install-ctl resolves paths from artifacts.toml. I'll replace the old cargo invocation logic with a single call to install-ctl, and I need a resolve_install_ctl() function that checks for install-ctl on PATH first, then falls back to running it via `cargo run` from the tools/install/install-ctl directory if needed.

When invoking install-ctl, I can pass the selected tools as separate positional arguments directly — `install-ctl install "${selected_tools[@]}"` — since the Command::Install selection expects a Vec<String> and each element is treated as a separate token, so no CSV joining is necessary. After install-ctl runs, I should preserve the exit code for behavior parity, though the instruction focuses mainly on CLI syntax and exit codes rather than identical summary text formatting.

The key difference is that the old install-tools.sh continues installing all selected tools even if one fails (using `|| true`), then exits 1 at the end with a summary and retry command, whereas install-ctl calls fail() and exits immediately on the first failure. I need to check how run_install in install-ctl handles this to understand whether I need to adjust the failure behavior. The wrapper's exit code semantics will still align with the original script's behavior—returning 0 only if all tools succeed and non-zero if any fail—because install-ctl propagates its exit code through to us. Even though install-ctl stops at the first failure rather than attempting all tools, the end result for exit codes matches what matters: success or failure signaling. Since the requirements focus on exit code parity rather than identical output formatting, delegating to install-ctl and passing through its exit status fits the spirit of a thin wrapper.

Actually, I can preserve the full original behavior by looping through each selected tool in the wrapper itself, invoking install-ctl once per tool, collecting the results, and then printing the same summary format using the existing installer_print_summary function from common.sh. This way I get both the correct exit code semantics and the exact partial-continue-on-failure behavior with the familiar summary output.

So I'll keep the tool_names and mcp_tool_names arrays since they're needed for validation, the --list flag, and --mcp expansion, along with all the selection parsing logic. But I can drop tool_path() and tool_bin() since install-ctl and artifacts.toml handle those lookups now.

For install_one(), I'll make it a wrapper that finds install-ctl (checking PATH first, then falling back to building it via cargo run from the Cargo.toml), then delegates the actual install to it with the appropriate flags like --dry-run and --no-force, capturing the exit code the same way. I'll use run_filtered_command from common.sh to display progress, matching how the original wrapped the cargo invocation.

Now I'm writing out the new install-tools.sh script, and I need to handle the --list output to show supported tools. The list matches perfectly with the 24 Rust binary artifacts in artifacts.toml, and ticket-vscode is correctly excluded since it belongs in install-extensions.sh, not install-tools.sh. Now I'll write out the updated file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Thin bootstrap-and-invoke wrapper around install-ctl (tools/install/install-ctl).
# All install mechanics (path/bin resolution, process-stop-before-install,
# CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation) live in install-ctl and its runtime-read
# tools/install/artifacts.toml registry; this script only preserves the
# existing CLI selection syntax and per-tool summary/exit-code behavior.

script_dir=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
repo_root=$script_dir
common_install_helpers="$repo_root/tools/install/common.sh"

if [[ ! -f "$common_install_helpers" ]]; then
    printf 'error: missing shared installer helpers: %s\n' "$common_install_helpers" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# shellcheck source=tools/install/common.sh
source "$common_install_helpers"

tool_names=(
    viewer-ctl
    doc-viewer
    log-viewer
    spec-viewer
    ticket-viewer
    copilot-capture-hook
    ticket-cli
    spec-cli
    audit-cli
    rule-cli
    feedback-cli
    session-cli
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
)

mcp_tool_names=(
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
    log-viewer
)

# Locate install-ctl: prefer an already-installed binary on PATH, otherwise
# run it straight from source via cargo (no separate build step required).
resolve_install_ctl() {
    if command -v install-ctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'install-ctl\n'
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'cargo run --manifest-path %q/tools/install/install-ctl/Cargo.toml --quiet --\n' "$repo_root"
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./install-tools.sh [options] [tool ...]

Install selected workspace tools with cargo install --path.

This script installs only deliverables built from this repository. External
toolchain dependencies are handled by ./install-deps.sh.

Options:
  --tool <name>       Install one tool; repeatable.
  --tools <a,b,c>     Install a comma-separated list of tools.
  --mcp               Install all MCP binaries configured for VS Code.
  --all               Install all supported tools.
  --list              Print supported tools and exit.
  --dry-run           Print the cargo install commands without running them.
  --no-force          Do not pass --force to cargo install.
  -h, --help          Show this help text.

EOF

    printf 'Supported tools:\n'
    print_supported_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    printf '\nMCP tools (--mcp):\n'
    print_mcp_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    cat <<'EOF'

Environment:
  INSTALL_TOOLS       Comma-separated tool list used when no tools are passed.

Examples:
  ./install-tools.sh
  ./install-tools.sh spec-cli ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool viewer-ctl --tool ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool doc-viewer --tool log-viewer --tool spec-viewer --tool ticket-viewer
  ./install-tools.sh --tool audit-cli --tool rule-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool mcp-toolmon
  ./install-tools.sh --mcp
  INSTALL_TOOLS="rule-cli,spec-cli" ./install-tools.sh --dry-run
EOF
}

print_supported_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

print_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

contains_tool() {
    local needle=$1
    shift

    local item
    for item in "$@"; do
        if [[ "$item" == "$needle" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    return 1
}

append_tool() {
    local tool=$1

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${tool_names[@]}"; then
        printf 'error: unsupported tool: %s\n' "$tool" >&2
        printf 'supported tools:\n' >&2
        print_supported_tools >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${selected_tools[@]}"; then
        selected_tools+=("$tool")
    fi
}

append_csv_tools() {
    local csv=$1
    local item

    IFS=',' read -r -a csv_tools <<< "$csv"
    for item in "${csv_tools[@]}"; do
        item=${item//[[:space:]]/}
        [[ -n "$item" ]] || continue
        append_tool "$item"
    done
}

append_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
}

selected_tools=()
installed_tools=()
failed_tools=()
force_install=1
dry_run=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --tool)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tool requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_tool "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --tools)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tools requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_csv_tools "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --all)
            selected_tools=()
            for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
                append_tool "$tool"
            done
            shift
            ;;
        --mcp)
            append_mcp_tools
            shift
            ;;
        --list)
            print_supported_tools
            exit 0
            ;;
        --dry-run)
            dry_run=1
            shift
            ;;
        --no-force)
            force_install=0
            shift
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            usage
            exit 0
            ;;
        --)
            shift
            while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
                append_tool "$1"
                shift
            done
            break
            ;;
        -*)
            printf 'error: unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        *)
            append_tool "$1"
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 && -n "${INSTALL_TOOLS:-}" ]]; then
    append_csv_tools "$INSTALL_TOOLS"
fi

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
fi

install_ctl_cmd=$(resolve_install_ctl)

install_one() {
    local tool=$1
    local failed=0
    local -a install_ctl_args=(install "$tool")

    if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args+=(--no-force)
    fi
    if [[ $dry_run -eq 1 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args=(--dry-run "${install_ctl_args[@]}")
    fi

    printf '==> %s\n' "$tool"

    if ! (
        cd "$repo_root"
        eval "$install_ctl_cmd" "\${install_ctl_args[@]@Q}"
    ); then
        failed=1
    fi

    if [[ $failed -eq 0 ]]; then
        installed_tools+=("$tool")
        return 0
    fi

    failed_tools+=("$tool")
    printf 'error: install failed for %s\n' "$tool" >&2
    return 1
}

for tool in "${selected_tools[@]}"; do
    install_one "$tool" || true
done

retry_prefix="./install-tools.sh"
if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
    retry_prefix="$retry_prefix --no-force"
fi

if ! installer_print_summary "${#selected_tools[@]}" installed_tools failed_tools "$retry_prefix" "./install-tools.sh --help"; then
    exit 1
fi

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Thin bootstrap-and-invoke wrapper around install-ctl (tools/install/install-ctl).
# All install mechanics (path/bin resolution, process-stop-before-install,
# CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation) live in install-ctl and its runtime-read
# tools/install/artifacts.toml registry; this script only preserves the
# existing CLI selection syntax and per-tool summary/exit-code behavior.

script_dir=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
repo_root=$script_dir
common_install_helpers="$repo_root/tools/install/common.sh"

if [[ ! -f "$common_install_helpers" ]]; then
    printf 'error: missing shared installer helpers: %s\n' "$common_install_helpers" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# shellcheck source=tools/install/common.sh
source "$common_install_helpers"

tool_names=(
    viewer-ctl
    doc-viewer
    log-viewer
    spec-viewer
    ticket-viewer
    copilot-capture-hook
    ticket-cli
    spec-cli
    audit-cli
    rule-cli
    feedback-cli
    session-cli
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
)

mcp_tool_names=(
    context-mcp
    ticket-mcp
    spec-mcp
    test-mcp
    feedback-mcp
    session-mcp
    peek-mcp
    rule-mcp
    audit-mcp
    compact-terminal-mcp
    fs-mcp
    mcp-toolmon
    log-viewer
)

# Locate install-ctl: prefer an already-installed binary on PATH, otherwise
# run it straight from source via cargo (no separate build step required).
resolve_install_ctl() {
    if command -v install-ctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'install-ctl\n'
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'cargo run --manifest-path %q/tools/install/install-ctl/Cargo.toml --quiet --\n' "$repo_root"
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ./install-tools.sh [options] [tool ...]

Install selected workspace tools with cargo install --path.

This script installs only deliverables built from this repository. External
toolchain dependencies are handled by ./install-deps.sh.

Options:
  --tool <name>       Install one tool; repeatable.
  --tools <a,b,c>     Install a comma-separated list of tools.
  --mcp               Install all MCP binaries configured for VS Code.
  --all               Install all supported tools.
  --list              Print supported tools and exit.
  --dry-run           Print the cargo install commands without running them.
  --no-force          Do not pass --force to cargo install.
  -h, --help          Show this help text.

EOF

    printf 'Supported tools:\n'
    print_supported_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    printf '\nMCP tools (--mcp):\n'
    print_mcp_tools | sed 's/^/  /'

    cat <<'EOF'

Environment:
  INSTALL_TOOLS       Comma-separated tool list used when no tools are passed.

Examples:
  ./install-tools.sh
  ./install-tools.sh spec-cli ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool viewer-ctl --tool ticket-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool doc-viewer --tool log-viewer --tool spec-viewer --tool ticket-viewer
  ./install-tools.sh --tool audit-cli --tool rule-cli
  ./install-tools.sh --tool mcp-toolmon
  ./install-tools.sh --mcp
  INSTALL_TOOLS="rule-cli,spec-cli" ./install-tools.sh --dry-run
EOF
}

print_supported_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

print_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        printf '%s\n' "$tool"
    done
}

contains_tool() {
    local needle=$1
    shift

    local item
    for item in "$@"; do
        if [[ "$item" == "$needle" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    return 1
}

append_tool() {
    local tool=$1

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${tool_names[@]}"; then
        printf 'error: unsupported tool: %s\n' "$tool" >&2
        printf 'supported tools:\n' >&2
        print_supported_tools >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if ! contains_tool "$tool" "${selected_tools[@]}"; then
        selected_tools+=("$tool")
    fi
}

append_csv_tools() {
    local csv=$1
    local item

    IFS=',' read -r -a csv_tools <<< "$csv"
    for item in "${csv_tools[@]}"; do
        item=${item//[[:space:]]/}
        [[ -n "$item" ]] || continue
        append_tool "$item"
    done
}

append_mcp_tools() {
    local tool

    for tool in "${mcp_tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
}

selected_tools=()
installed_tools=()
failed_tools=()
force_install=1
dry_run=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --tool)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tool requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_tool "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --tools)
            [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || {
                printf 'error: --tools requires a value\n' >&2
                exit 1
            }
            append_csv_tools "$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --all)
            selected_tools=()
            for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
                append_tool "$tool"
            done
            shift
            ;;
        --mcp)
            append_mcp_tools
            shift
            ;;
        --list)
            print_supported_tools
            exit 0
            ;;
        --dry-run)
            dry_run=1
            shift
            ;;
        --no-force)
            force_install=0
            shift
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            usage
            exit 0
            ;;
        --)
            shift
            while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
                append_tool "$1"
                shift
            done
            break
            ;;
        -*)
            printf 'error: unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        *)
            append_tool "$1"
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 && -n "${INSTALL_TOOLS:-}" ]]; then
    append_csv_tools "$INSTALL_TOOLS"
fi

if [[ ${#selected_tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    for tool in "${tool_names[@]}"; do
        append_tool "$tool"
    done
fi

install_ctl_cmd=$(resolve_install_ctl)

install_one() {
    local tool=$1
    local failed=0
    local -a install_ctl_args=(install "$tool")

    if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args+=(--no-force)
    fi
    if [[ $dry_run -eq 1 ]]; then
        install_ctl_args=(--dry-run "${install_ctl_args[@]}")
    fi

    printf '==> %s\n' "$tool"

    if ! (
        cd "$repo_root"
        eval "$install_ctl_cmd" "\${install_ctl_args[@]@Q}"
    ); then
        failed=1
    fi

    if [[ $failed -eq 0 ]]; then
        installed_tools+=("$tool")
        return 0
    fi

    failed_tools+=("$tool")
    printf 'error: install failed for %s\n' "$tool" >&2
    return 1
}

for tool in "${selected_tools[@]}"; do
    install_one "$tool" || true
done

retry_prefix="./install-tools.sh"
if [[ $force_install -eq 0 ]]; then
    retry_prefix="$retry_prefix --no-force"
fi

if ! installer_print_summary "${#selected_tools[@]}" installed_tools failed_tools "$retry_prefix" "./install-tools.sh --help"; then
    exit 1
fi

resolve_installed_extension_dir() {
    local extension=$1
    local publisher_and_name=${extension_id[$extension]:-}
    local extensions_root=${HOME}/.vscode/extensions

    if [[ -z "$publisher_and_name" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    if [[ ! -d "$extensions_root" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    local matches=()
    local candidate
    for candidate in "$extensions_root"/"$publisher_and_name"-*; do
        [[ -d "$candidate" ]] || continue
        matches+=("$candidate")
    done

    if [[ ${#matches[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "${matches[@]}" | sort | tail -n 1
}

GREP_OUTPUT=$(grep -rn "viewer-ctl" --exclude-dir=target --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.session --exclude-dir=.benchmark --exclude-dir=.test --exclude-dir=.spec . 2>/dev/null | grep -v "^\./viewer-api/viewer-ctl/" || true)

echo "===GREP_RAW_BEGIN==="
echo "$GREP_OUTPUT"
echo "===GREP_RAW_END==="

# Group by file with counts and representative lines
echo "===GREP_GROUPED_BEGIN==="
if [ -z "$GREP_OUTPUT" ]; then
  echo "NO_MATCHES"
else
  echo "$GREP_OUTPUT" | awk -F":" '{file=$1; line=$2; $1=""; $2=""; sub(/^:/,""); sub(/^:/,""); content=substr($0,3); cnt[file]++; lines[file]=lines[file] sprintf("  %s: %s\n",line,content)} END{ for (f in cnt){ if(cnt[f]>8){ print f " = " cnt[f]; n=0; split(lines[f], arr, "\n"); for(i=1;i<=5;i++){ if(arr[i]!="") print arr[i] } print "  ... (" cnt[f] " matches)" } else { print f " = " cnt[f]; split(lines[f], arr, "\n"); for(i in arr) if(arr[i]!="") print arr[i] } } }'

# 4) viewer-ctl.toml existence and line counts, and diff

ROOT_EXISTS=0; SUB_EXISTS=0
if [ -f viewer-ctl.toml ]; then ROOT_EXISTS=1; ROOT_LINES=$(wc -l < viewer-ctl.toml); else ROOT_LINES=missing; fi
if [ -f viewer-api/viewer-ctl.toml ]; then SUB_EXISTS=1; SUB_LINES=$(wc -l < viewer-api/viewer-ctl.toml); else SUB_LINES=missing; fi

if [ $ROOT_EXISTS -eq 1 ] && [ $SUB_EXISTS -eq 1 ]; then if diff -q viewer-ctl.toml viewer-api/viewer-ctl.toml >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "IDENTICAL=yes"; else echo "IDENTICAL=no"; fi; else echo "IDENTICAL=no"; fi
echo "===VIEWER_CTL_TOML_END==="

echo "===VIEWER_API_GIT_BEGIN==="
if [ -d viewer-api/.git ] || [ -d viewer-api ]; then git -C viewer-api status --short 2>/dev/null || true; git -C viewer-api rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true; git -C viewer-api rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true; git -C viewer-api branch -a 2>/dev/null || true; else echo "viewer-api missing"; fi

```bash
install-ctl viewer stop doc-viewer

# log-viewer  — http://localhost:3000
install-ctl start log-viewer --no-build &
sleep 2 && curl -sf http://localhost:3000/ -o /dev/null && echo "log-viewer OK"
install-ctl viewer stop log-viewer

install-ctl start ticket-viewer --no-build &
sleep 2 && curl -sf http://localhost:3002/ -o /dev/null && echo "ticket-viewer OK"
install-ctl viewer stop ticket-viewer

# spec-viewer — http://localhost:4002
install-ctl start spec-viewer --no-build &
sleep 2 && curl -sf http://localhost:4002/ -o /dev/null && echo "spec-viewer OK"
install-ctl viewer stop spec-viewer
```

## Tool Use Examples

### Install the viewer toolchain

From the `context-engine` repo root, install the lifecycle manager and WASM frontend builder together:

```bash
bash ./install-tools.sh --tool viewer-ctl --tool trunk
```

If you are working from a standalone `memory-viewers/viewer-api` checkout, use Cargo directly from this workspace:

```bash
cargo install --path viewer-ctl --bin viewer-ctl
cargo install trunk
```

After that, `viewer-ctl prepare ...` can build the Dioxus frontends because the `trunk` command is on `PATH`.

- `viewer-ctl list`, `viewer-ctl start`, and `viewer-ctl prepare` are documented in [viewer-ctl/README.md](viewer-ctl/README.md).
- The shared backend runtime checked with `cargo check -p viewer-api` is documented in [viewer-api/README.md](viewer-api/README.md).
- The frontend `trunk serve` and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p viewer-api-dioxus` flows are documented in [viewer-api/frontend/dioxus/README.md](viewer-api/frontend/dioxus/README.md).

| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewer-api` | Shared HTTP and MCP runtime for viewer tools, including auth, middleware, pagination, query/session helpers, source adapters, SSE, static file serving, and tracing setup. | Rust library consumed by viewer servers |
| `viewer-ctl` | Config-driven lifecycle manager for viewer components declared in `viewer-ctl.toml`. | `viewer-ctl list`, `viewer-ctl start`, `viewer-ctl prepare` |
| `viewer-api-dioxus` | Dioxus viewer platform scaffold with the root app, WebGPU canvas, UI overlay shell, and shared frontend building blocks. | `trunk serve`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p viewer-api-dioxus` |

## Tool Use Examples

### Install the viewer toolchain

From the `context-engine` repo root, install the lifecycle manager and WASM frontend builder together:

```bash
bash ./install-tools.sh --tool viewer-ctl --tool trunk
```

If you are working from a standalone `memory-viewers/viewer-api` checkout, use Cargo directly from this workspace:

```bash
cargo install --path viewer-ctl --bin viewer-ctl
cargo install trunk
```

After that, `viewer-ctl prepare ...` can build the Dioxus frontends because the `trunk` command is on `PATH`.

- `viewer-ctl list`, `viewer-ctl start`, and `viewer-ctl prepare` are documented in [viewer-ctl/README.md](viewer-ctl/README.md).
- The shared backend runtime checked with `cargo check -p viewer-api` is documented in [viewer-api/README.md](viewer-api/README.md).
- The frontend `trunk serve` and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p viewer-api-dioxus` flows are documented in [viewer-api/frontend/dioxus/README.md](viewer-api/frontend/dioxus/README.md).

```bash
viewer-ctl list
viewer-ctl start spec-viewer
cargo check -p viewer-api
cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p viewer-api-dioxus
```

- Inspect which viewer components are declared in `viewer-ctl.toml`.
- Start a configured viewer through the lifecycle manager.
- Validate the shared backend runtime in `viewer-api`.
- Validate the shared browser scaffold in `viewer-api-dioxus`.

The issue is that even though the merge is technically fast-forward capable, git will reject it because the working tree has uncommitted changes to `install-tools.sh` and the merge would overwrite that file. Git's protection against losing local changes operates at the file level rather than checking individual hunks, so it refuses the operation outright.

The user's local edits add `mcp-toolmon` to the tool_names array and reorder it, but the branch heavily rewrites that section—removing 79 lines and adding 23—which means their changes would need reconciliation. Since the branch now delegates to install-ctl and reads from artifacts.toml, the tool_names array might still exist but the registry becomes authoritative, making the user's manual reordering potentially obsolete or a signal about artifact ordering they want preserved. I need to ask the user directly what they want to do rather than stashing or discarding their work.
